correction: PARTIAL is right, but two of the auditor's claims are too strong: that "the core serialization is gone" and that there is "no concrete defect". (1) The app document and assets are still served by the backend process. The early static handler runs on the backend's event loop, and migrations run synchronously there (node:sqlite DatabaseSync). So a stall while the runtime graph builds still stops the renderer from fetching any app JS. The user's own desktop-main.log after #710 shows 2 of 16 launches where the early-loaded document took 15-18 s to reach dom-ready (server-child.log: 'persistence.migrations (18040 ms, in flight)' plus an event-loop stall). During those stalls the 45f7a9be6 last-known shell could not paint. (2) The bind-time load usually starts about 65-75 ms after the boot page load and aborts it before it commits: boot dom-ready never fired in 14 of 16 launches. During a stall, the reveal fallback then shows a blank window (run 2a6031c40a6b: 'reveal-fallback urlKind=blank' at 428 ms, app dom-ready at 15188 ms). Before #710 the boot splash was visible during stalls. (3) The 9 s staleness heuristic counts from the load request, not from the document's commit, so a document that loaded fine just before ready is reloaded anyway (same run: app dom-ready at 15188 ms, reload at 18386 ms). The auditor's point that 'a slow spawn or bind shows only the boot page' is also inaccurate: the boot page usually never commits.
summary: Implemented differently, and only in part. The packaged window now loads http://127.0.0.1:PORT when the backend sends `http-bound`, and the backend serves the static shell from its startup gate. The backend is spawned from desktopEntry before the main bundle loads. Together these remove the wait for 'Listening' on normal launches: in the user's logs, window.create to bind is about 100 ms (82-242 ms) and bind to serving about 20-170 ms. The ryco://app proposal was not implemented. The ryco:// scheme is still registered with codeCache through the deprecated registerFileProtocol and is used only as a boot-page fallback. The origin is still http://127.0.0.1:PORT (3773 legacy for existing installs, 7926 for new ones). The shell document still comes from the backend process, so the proposal's main benefit is not achieved: painting cached state through backend stalls. Real launches after #710 show 15-18 s migration stalls on update launches, during which no app document was served. The bind-time load also introduced a blank-window regression during such stalls, plus a redundant reload at ready.

evidence.note: The `http-bound` lifecycle frame calls loadPackagedBackendAppWindowOnBind(), so the app load starts when the port is bound, not at ready.

loadPackagedBackendAppWindow(…, moment) still does window.loadURL(backendHttpUrl) at line 1757, so the document comes from the backend process. The load is gated on rendererCacheMaintenance (line 1752), which waits up to 1.5 s for clearCodeCaches on a version change (line 4773).
The early static handler (desktop mode serves `/` and assets) runs on the backend's own event loop while the gate is closed, and writes the `http-bound` frame at line 295.
Migrations and SQLite access use synchronous node:sqlite DatabaseSync on the backend main thread. A heavy migration blocks the same loop that must serve the early shell.

Run 2a6031c40a6b: bound 243 ms, app load-request 243 ms, reveal-fallback urlKind=blank at 428 ms, app dom-ready 15188 ms, listening 18386 ms, a second app load at ready, dom-ready 18459 ms. Run 57fddc1a1b24: app dom-ready 16005 ms. In server-child.log the same run shows migrations 087/088 taking 18040 ms with an event-loop stall warning.

In the other 14 runs: window.create to http-bound median about 100 ms (82-242), bind to serving 21-441 ms, launch to shell-usable 534-1442 ms. The boot page never reached dom-ready before the bind-time load replaced it in 14/16 runs.
The boot page load is followed by a 250 ms reveal fallback that reveals the window even when urlKind is 'blank', which is what happens when the early app navigation aborted the uncommitted boot page.
EARLY_APP_LOAD_MAX_HOLD_MS = 9 s is measured from requestedAtMs, not from document commit, so a document that loaded late but correctly is reloaded at ready.
Held requests get a 503 after 10 s. The client gives up control-plane bootstrap retries after 15 s with a 5 s per-request deadline. Stalls longer than this need the desktop reload at ready.

primary-shell-usable (which the desktop uses as shellUsable) is marked only when a live snapshot is applied. A cached-shell paint does not count, so a failed early boot is reloaded rather than reconnected. This is correct.
The early backend spawn happens before desktopMain.cjs loads, which shrinks the remaining window.create-to-bind gap to about 100 ms.
ryco:// is privileged with codeCache but registered through the deprecated protocol.registerFileProtocol. It is used only as a boot-page fallback. The boot page loads through loadFile (file://).
The origin is still port-bound. Installs with prior renderer state keep legacy port 3773 (T3 Code's default; the user's logs show port=3773), so a busy port still flips the origin for that launch.

remaining: (1) Biggest residual: the renderer document and boot graph are still served by the backend process (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1757 loads backendHttpUrl, served by the early handler at apps/server/src/server.ts:276-299 on the backend event loop). An event-loop-blocking stall in the runtime graph, such as synchronous node:sqlite migrations on the first launch after an update, still stops the renderer from fetching or parsing any app JS. The cached primary shell (45f7a9be6) therefore cannot paint during exactly the 15-18 s stalls the finding targeted (2 of 16 logged launches after #710). (2) On normal launches the app load still starts at bind, about 100 ms (82-242 ms) after window creation. The window starts on a file:// boot page and swaps to a cross-site http renderer (main.ts:4375-4382 → 1757). (3) The origin is still http://127.0.0.1:PORT (backendPort.ts). The ryco:// codeCache privilege and the deprecated registerFileProtocol (main.ts:337-350, 2196) are effectively unused. (4) Related: on a version change the first app load waits up to 1.5 s for clearCodeCaches (main.ts:1752, 4773).
fixDefects: (a) Blank window during stalls: in 14 of 16 launches the bind-time loadURL (main.ts:1757, about 65-75 ms after the boot load request) aborts the not-yet-committed file:// boot page. If the backend then stalls before serving the document, schedulePackagedBootReveal (main.ts:2483-2499) reveals a blank window. Run 2a6031c40a6b stayed blank for about 15 s (reveal-fallback urlKind=blank at 428 ms, app dom-ready at 15188 ms) instead of showing the boot splash it showed before #710. (b) Redundant reload: isAppLoadRequestCurrent (backendAppWindowLoad.ts:44-56) ages the early load from requestedAtMs. After a stall longer than 9 s, ready reloads a document that committed seconds earlier and whose held requests cannot have hit the 10 s 503 yet (same run: dom-ready at 15188 ms, reload at 18386 ms). The cost is about 250 ms plus a re-boot and a flash. (c) The 'bound' path is skipped in development (main.ts:1768), so dev builds never exercise it. That is minor but worth a test hook.
implementationSketch: Step 1 (S, no decision needed), fix the early-load defects in apps/desktop/src/main.ts and backendAppWindowLoad.ts. (i) Keep a pending app navigation from leaving the window blank: when the reveal fallback fires with urlKind 'blank' while appLoadRequestedFrom has a current request, or when the app navigation has not committed within about 750 ms (track 'did-start-navigation'/'did-navigate' for backendHttpUrl), stop it and call loadDesktopBootPage(window). Delete the appLoadRequestedFrom entry so `ready` loads the app, reusing returnEarlyLoadedWindowsToBootPage's logic. An alternative that keeps the early load is to delay the bound-time loadURL until the boot page's dom-ready, capped at about 100 ms. That costs 0-50 ms on normal launches but keeps the splash visible, because Chromium keeps the committed boot page during the pending navigation. (ii) Age early loads from document commit or dom-ready, not the request: record committedAtMs in AppLoadRequest from 'did-navigate', and treat the request as current while now - (committedAtMs ?? requestedAtMs) < EARLY_APP_LOAD_MAX_HOLD_MS. Add cases to backendAppWindowLoad.test.ts, and assert in boot-report.mjs and startup-timing-smoke.mjs that 'desktop.window.boot.reveal-fallback urlKind=blank' never occurs. Step 2 (M, needs a decision), decouple the shell document from the backend process. The recommended option keeps the origin: in registerDesktopProtocol, use protocol.handle('http') on the default session (Electron 44) only during boot. Serve GET `/`, `/index.html` and `/assets/*` for exactly backendHttpUrl's origin from the bundled static dir, sharing resolveDesktopStaticPath and the path-safety checks with the ryco:// handler. Pass everything else through net.fetch(request, { bypassCustomProtocolHandlers: true }). Call protocol.unhandle('http') at http-serving so steady-state API traffic never hops through main. WebSocket traffic is not intercepted. With that in place, call loadURL(backendHttpUrl) directly from createWindow, so there is no boot page in the normal path. The cached primary shell (same origin, same localStorage/IndexedDB) paints during migrations. Primary bootstrap requests get ECONNREFUSED or are held and retried (primaryAuth retryTransientBootstrap). Extend the desktop path so the renderer keeps retrying, or rely on notifyRenderersToReconnect at ready, instead of failing after 15 s. Test with a fixture home that forces a slow migration, and check shell-usable, primary-cached-sidebar-committed and the absence of a blank reveal in desktop-main.log. Step 3 (L, optional; switching to ryco://app is what fixes the origin): implement the original ryco://app plan. Switch the scheme handler to protocol.handle. Allow ryco://app in browserApiCorsLayer and the WS upgrade origin check. Use bearer/DPoP for the desktop primary environment. Run a one-time migration of origin-scoped storage (composer drafts, primary shell cache, UI state). Drop the codeCache privilege and registerFileProtocol if it is not pursued. Optionally move the version-change clearCodeCaches off the first-load path (main.ts:1752).
decisionReason: Step 1, the blank-window and redundant-reload fixes, needs no decision. Decoupling the shell from the backend does: either intercept the http backend origin in the Electron session during boot, which is a new security-relevant request path in main, or move to ryco://app. The latter changes desktop primary-environment auth (cookie to bearer/DPoP), adds a CORS/WS origin allowlist entry and needs an origin-storage migration, which calls for a security review and a product trade-off against modest normal-path gains (about 100 ms) and stall-only benefits (update launches with heavy migrations).
